text:
Maya: Heads up — seeing a cluster of OOM spikes on prod-gpu-3 after the kernel routing update at ~03:10 UTC. 3 failed requests, all during long-chat paths (seq_len ~2048).
Maya: Quick grep of dmesg shows fragmentation growth before OOM: 
```
[warn] cuda_alloc: free list fragmentation 78%
[info] kv_cache: reserved 1.2GB, active 3.8GB
```
Aj: Hmm. Did the routing change also move some requests to the (new) fwd-optimized kernels? Those tend to change workspace sizing.
Maya: Yes — routing sent more large-seq requests to kernel-v2 (fwd-optim). I suspect different workspace layout + our allocator knobs interacted badly.
Simon: Can you share the current per-device allocator config? Also which knobs we changed last week?
Maya: Current snapshot we deployed:
```
expandable_segments: true
max_split_size_mb: 128
garbage_collection_threshold: 0.3
buffer_reuse_enabled: true
```
Maya: We rolled expandable_segments=true in the same deploy as kernel-v2.
Aj: That combo can increase small-chunk churn. expandable_segments helps avoid big GC pauses but can create many small free slots that max_split_size affects.
Aj: Try a quick canary: set max_split_size_mb=64 and gc_threshold=0.45 on one host and run the same repro traffic.
Simon: I ran that locally against the reproducer container — results: 5 runs, baseline 3/5 OOMs, canary 1/5 OOM. Latency impact negligible (+~2ms p50).
Simon: Reproducer command I used: 
```
PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64,garbage_collection_threshold:0.45 python -m stress_repro --seq 2048 --batches 10 --model redwood/gpt-big
```
alloc-bot: profilingsampled: host=prod-gpu-3 ts=2026-03-17T03:12:42Z peak_rss=12.1GB fragmentation_index=0.78 kv_cache_hits=0.92
Priya: We should consider per-model overrides in routing rules so large-seq models get tighter max_split_size and higher gc thresholds. That avoids global regressions.
Priya: Proposal for rollout: 1) Canary per-host knob patch (64/0.45) on 2 hosts 2) Run synthetic long-seq traffic for 2 hours 3) If OOM rate drops <0.5%, ship policy that maps models with seq>1024 to the new knob set.
Aj: I can draft the small allocator patch to allow dynamic knob toggles per-routing-tag. Pseudocode: 
```
if request.tag == 'long_seq':
  set_allocator_knobs(max_split=64, gc_thresh=0.45)
else:
  set_allocator_knobs(max_split=128, gc_thresh=0.3)
```
Aj: We'll need metrics: per-request OOM_count, fragmentation_index histogram, p50/p95 latency. Add an eval that asserts generation success >99%.
Maya: Will run the canary tonight and post results in morning. If canary looks good, we can do staged rollout.
Priya: also add a small stress test to CI that runs kernel-v1 and kernel-v2 combinations to catch this earlier.
Simon: One more data point — enabling buffer_reuse=false in the repro made OOMs worse (5/5), so reuse is still helpful; problem seems mainly fragmentation due to too-large split sizes.
Maya: thanks — updating runbook and kicking off canary now. Will @here when done :thumbsup:
